notes: STAND-IN (read as its own source, not used to confirm the article): Duarte, C. M. 1987. Biomass and distribution of submerged macrophytes in lakes. PhD thesis, McGill University (docs/research_notes/fetched/v2/Duarte_1987.pdf; its own evidence file is Duarte_1987.json). Chapter III, 'The distribution of submerged macrophyte biomass in lakes: the contribution of littoral morphometry and water characteristics' (PDF p. 78), studies 25 north-eastern American lakes (Québec, New York, Vermont; August 1985; 187 sites). On p. 81 (PDF p. 94, read on the page image) it gives the shallowest depth with submerged vegetation as 0.75–1.25 m and says 'this minimum depth is not related to slope, exposure or transparency (P > 0.05)', 'suggesting that the shallow limit is probably set by ice scouring' — an inference, not a measurement. Caveat for both §3.4.4 and §5.6: the echosounder transects started at 'a depth of c. 0.7 m' (p. 69, PDF p. 82), so the survey could not see plants shallower than about that depth. The thesis preface (PDF p. 11) says chapters I and II were published (CJFAS 43: 1900–1908; L&O 31: 1072–1080) and chapters III and IV were 'submitted for publication'. Recommendation: cite 'Duarte 1987' for the 0.75–1.25-m minimum and the ice-scour inference, and cite Duarte & Kalff 1990 only after its text is read.
